hook_q: How does mutual consent divorce work?

slides.title: Three things you **must show.**
list: You've lived separately for one year or more
You have not been able to live together
You both agree the marriage should end

slides.title: File **together** in district court.
slides.body: Both spouses file one joint petition in the district court where you married, where you last lived together, or where the wife now lives.

timeline.text: If the petition isn't withdrawn, you make a **second joint motion.**
After hearing you and any inquiry, the court can **dissolve the marriage** from the decree's date.

slides.title: Consent must be **genuine.**
slides.body: The court must be satisfied that consent was not obtained by force, fraud or undue influence.

slides.title: Can the 6 months be **waived?**
list: Yes, the court may waive it, considering:
1 year's separation + 6 months over before first motion
Genuine settlement, incl. alimony and child custody
Waiting would only prolong your agony
slides.ref: Supreme Court · Amardeep Singh v Harveen Kaur (2017), quoted in Shilpa Sailesh (2023)
slides.note: Ask one week after first motion

slides.title: Special Marriage Act? **Same timeline.**
slides.body: For marriages under the Special Marriage Act, the joint petition also needs one year's separation, and the second motion comes 6 to 18 months after filing.

slides.title: Uttarakhand? **Different law.**
slides.body: The Hindu Marriage Act covers Hindus, Buddhists, Jains and Sikhs (not Scheduled Tribes unless notified). For Uttarakhand residents (except Scheduled Tribes), the State's Uniform Civil Code now applies instead.
slides.ref: Hindu Marriage Act 1955 · Sec 2; UCC Rules, Uttarakhand, 2025 · Rules 1(3), 2

sources: Supreme Court of India – Shilpa Sailesh v. Varun Sreenivasan, [2023] 5 S.C.R. 165 (1 May 2023), quoting Amardeep Singh v. Harveen Kaur (2017) (digiscr.sci.gov.in)
Uniform Civil Code Rules, Uttarakhand, 2025 – Rules 1(3), 2 (ucc.uk.gov.in)
caption:
Both of you want to end the marriage? Here's how mutual consent divorce works. 👇

1️⃣ You must have lived separately for one year or more, and both agree the marriage should end
2️⃣ File one joint petition in the district court
3️⃣ Make a second joint motion 6 to 18 months later, if the petition isn't withdrawn
4️⃣ The court must be satisfied your consent wasn't obtained by force, fraud or undue influence
5️⃣ The Supreme Court has held the 6-month wait can be waived by the court in suitable cases
6️⃣ The Special Marriage Act has the same one-year and 6–18 month timeline
⚠️ In Uttarakhand, the State's Uniform Civil Code, 2024 now applies to residents (except Scheduled Tribes)

Source: Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 (Sec 13B, 19, 23); Special Marriage Act, 1954 (Sec 28); Supreme Court, Shilpa Sailesh v. Varun Sreenivasan (2023)
